Imagine a self-contained, hypothetical world with only the following conditions, and without any unmentioned factors or causal relationships: Hwax has a direct effect on gyzp and jyka. Jyka has a direct effect on lirg. Gyzp has a direct effect on lirg. Method 1: We look at how jyka correlates with lirg case by case according to gyzp. Method 2: We look directly at how jyka correlates with lirg in general. To understand how jyka affects lirg, is it more correct to use the Method 1 than Method 2?

action.content:
Yes

In this hypothetical world, $Hwax$ acts as a confounder because it has direct causal paths to both the treatment ($jyka$) and the outcome ($lirg$), creating a backdoor path: $jyka \leftarrow Hwax \rightarrow gyzp \rightarrow lirg$ (and potentially $jyka \leftarrow Hwax \rightarrow lirg$ if $Hwax$ affects $lirg$ directly, though the prompt specifies $Hwax \rightarrow gyzp$ and $gyzp \rightarrow lirg$, the key is that $Hwax$ influences the distribution of $gyzp$ which influences $lirg$, and $Hwax$ also influences $jyka$). More critically, since $Hwax$ affects $jyka$ and $gyzp$ (which affects $lirg$), there is a non-causal association between $jyka$ and $lirg$ induced by $Hwax$.

Method 2 calculates the marginal correlation between $jyka$ and $lirg$. Because $Hwax$ is a common cause of the variables in the causal chain leading to $lirg$ (via $gyzp$) and $jyka$, the marginal correlation will be biased by the confounding effect of $Hwax$. It conflates the true causal effect of $jyka$ on $lirg$ with the spurious correlation induced by $Hwax$.

Method 1 involves stratifying by $gyzp$ (looking at the correlation case by case according to $gyzp$). By conditioning on $gyzp$, we block the path from $Hwax$ to $lirg$ that flows through $gyzp$ ($Hwax \rightarrow gyzp \rightarrow lirg$). Since $gyzp$ is a mediator on the path from $Hwax$ to $lirg$, and $Hwax$ is the source of the confounding bias relative to the $jyka \rightarrow lirg$ relationship, conditioning on $gyzp$ isolates the variation in $lirg$ that is not explained by the $Hwax \rightarrow gyzp \rightarrow lirg$ pathway. Specifically, within strata of fixed $gyzp$, the effect of $Hwax$ on $lirg$ is held constant (blocked), allowing us to observe the direct effect of $jyka$ on $lirg$ without the bias introduced by the varying levels of $Hwax$ across the population. Therefore, Method 1 provides an unbiased estimate of the causal effect, while Method 2 does not.
